concept.title: About the DITA-OT Zensical plug-in
concept.shortdesc: Publish a DITA map as a Zensical site through an interchange format that keeps DITA processing separate from site generation.

conbody.p: The plug-in transforms a DITA map into a static site. DITA-OT handles keys, conrefs, filtering, chunking, and topic processing. A Python adapter converts the result into Markdown pages and Zensical configuration, then Zensical builds the site.

section.title: Build stages

ol.li: Interchange: DITA-OT writes XHTML5 topic fragments, JSON metadata, and a navigation model to out/interchange/. This stage does not depend on Zensical.
Sources: the Python adapter writes Markdown pages, images, CSS, and zensical.toml under out/docs/.
Site: Zensical turns those sources into the static site under out/site/.

section.p: Set zensical.stage to interchange or sources to stop after an earlier stage. The default, site, runs all three stages.
The interchange file format is described in the repository's INTERCHANGE.md.

section.title: HTML5 fragments serialized as XHTML
section.p: The plug-in uses DITA-OT's maintained HTML5 transformation for its vocabulary, including elements such as section, figure, and nav. It serializes each topic fragment as well-formed XHTML in the XHTML namespace. This lets the Python adapter use the standard XML parser while retaining the HTML5 structure.

section.title: Python adapter modules
section.p: The Python package separates interchange loading, theme adaptation, highlighting, page writing, and configuration writing. The interchange, theme, and highlighting modules handle the build data and DITA presentation. The page and configuration writers adapt those results to Zensical. This split keeps the DITA processing independent from the final site generator.

section.title: Next steps
section.p: Follow Build and preview the documentation to install the plug-in and generate a site. For options, see Build parameters and configuration.
